candidate_readme:
# Agent Trace

Exports the agent loop as an OpenTelemetry trace, written as OTLP/JSON lines
so a collector (`otlpjsonfile` receiver) or any OTLP-aware viewer can load it.

```bash
pi -e examples/extensions/agent-trace/index.ts
```

## File

`<sessionDir>/traces/<sessionId>.otlp.jsonl`, or `PI_AGENT_TRACE_FILE`. Every
line is one `ExportTraceServiceRequest` holding one span; resource attributes
carry `service.name`, `service.version`, `pi.session.id` and `process.pid`.
Every span has a start line immediately and an end line once its attributes
are known. Chat end lines are flushed at the first tool start (or `turn_end`
without tools); tool end lines wait for persisted entries at `turn_end`.
End lines follow end-time order and are never rewritten; `/reload` and later processes append to the same file with
the same trace id (derived from the session id).

## Spans

| name | kind | parent | attributes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `pi.run` | INTERNAL | root | `pi.run.trigger` (`prompt` / `wakeup` / `continuation`), `pi.run.turn_count`, `pi.session.entry_id` |
| `pi.turn` | INTERNAL | run | `pi.turn.index`, `pi.turn.stop_reason`, `pi.turn.tool_call_count` |
| `chat <model>` | CLIENT | turn | `gen_ai.operation.name`, `gen_ai.system`, `gen_ai.request.model`, `gen_ai.usage.input_tokens`, `gen_ai.usage.output_tokens`, `pi.usage.cache_read_tokens`, `pi.usage.cache_write_tokens`, `gen_ai.response.finish_reasons`, `pi.session.entry_id` |
| `execute_tool <name>` | INTERNAL | turn | `gen_ai.operation.name`, `gen_ai.tool.name`, `gen_ai.tool.call.id`, `pi.tool.is_error`, `pi.session.entry_id` |
| `pi.compaction` | INTERNAL | root | `pi.compaction.reason`, `pi.compaction.will_retry`, `pi.compaction.tokens_before`, `pi.session.entry_id` |

Status is ERROR (with a message) for failed tool results, error or aborted
assistant messages and the turns that contain them, and failed compactions.

User and custom follow-ups consumed within a run are listed in its steering
entry ids. A queued user or custom follow-up after `agent_end` but before
settling opens a continuation run referencing that message. An overflow retry
references its compaction instead. Error/aborted responses without an
`errorMessage` use status message `aborted`. Shutdown closes open spans as
`shutdown`; trace write failures are reported once as context-only messages.

## Child processes: cooperative tool integration

Inside a spawning tool's `execute(toolCallId, ...)`, request a private copy of
the child environment through pi's public extension event bus:

```ts
let childEnv: NodeJS.ProcessEnv | undefined;
pi.events.emit("agent-trace:child-env", {
  toolCallId,
  env: process.env, // optional base environment; copy any caller overrides here
  reply: (env: NodeJS.ProcessEnv | undefined) => { childEnv = env; },
});
if (!childEnv) throw new Error("No active traced tool for this call id");
// spawn imported from node:child_process; use your ordinary child arguments.
const child = spawn(process.execPath, childArgs, { env: childEnv });
```

The event handler replies synchronously. An unknown or ended call id returns
`undefined`; if the tracer is not loaded there is no reply. The copied env
contains `PI_AGENT_TRACE_PARENT=<traceId>-<toolSpanId>`. Load this extension in
the child too. It inherits that trace id, and both child runs and child
compactions attach directly to that tool. Each child uses its own session's
trace file by default; when supplying `PI_AGENT_TRACE_FILE`, choose a distinct
child path in the base environment.

Concurrent tools must each request their own `toolCallId`; context is never
stored in `process.env`, and requesting one tool's env cannot affect a sibling
or the parent. Tools without this integration still get ordinary tool spans,
but their child processes are not automatically attributed. The tracer uses
only public extension events and does not wrap core execution or serialize
tools. The runtime owns event subscriptions and removes them on reload.

Run the offline regression tests with `npm test -w packages/coding-agent`.
